target_customer: First-time homebuyers in the US (and the lenders who pay for referrals)
problem: Young buyers cannot tell what homes they can afford or find down payment assistance programs.
business_model: Marketplace referral fees from lenders (free mortgage comparison tool)
product_category: Mortgage and down payment assistance marketplace

founders.name: Malcolm-Wiley Floyd
previous_startups: two-time founder, earlier company not named

founders.name: Scott Fritz
founders.background_notes: YC page; the two met as roommates at Harvard per search results

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating mortgage products and a database of assistance programs is mostly data work with lender integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Program database is hard to compile but copyable; lender relationships are the real edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A similar down payment assistance finder (Quo) appeared in search results, undated.

market_need_then: Affordability pressure on first-time buyers; no dated spend figures found.

branding.domain_note: Uses stairsfinancial.com; stairs.com belongs to an unrelated stair parts retailer (site checked).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, buyer friendly (Find a home you can actually afford)

brand_strength.rationale: The stairs metaphor fits climbing the housing ladder (HousingWire/Online Marketplaces headline) but the generic word forced a longer domain; no community found.

outcome_analysis: Stairs launched its mortgage marketplace in late 2023 and announced a 3.5 million dollar seed in January 2024 led by Zigg Capital with YC and Antler. Aggregators list 3.6 to 4.2 million total and a few use past tense, but no source confirms a shutdown. The company looks active with a seed stage raise two years after the batch.
notes: Education for Floyd is null on the YC page; only the Harvard roommate claim from search results. Founding year reported 2020 (TechCrunch-style) or 2021 (YC). CB Insights says 4.15M over three rounds, another 3.62M; unverified. Past tense in aggregators only. HousingWire page fetch was rate limited. No dated competitor source found, list empty.
